tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> rests on a vertical post of height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. A bullet of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>, travelling in horizontal direction, hits the centre of the ball. After collision both travels independently. The ball hits the ground at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and the bullet at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the foot of the post. The value of initial velocity of the bullet will be (if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>) :

solution.text:
Let initial velocity of bullet be u.

Given, mass of bullet m=10 g and mass of ball M=200 g,

Initially ball is at height 5 m and at rest, the only acceleration acting is due to gravity.

Time of flight of each ball and bullet is t=2hg.

Now, velocity of ball and bullet as v1=302hg and v2=1202hg

As the collision is elastic, so applying conservation of linear momentum.

mu+M0=Mv1+mv2

⇒0.01u=0.230g2h+0.01120g2h

⇒u=300+60=360 m s-1
